newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady as market stays tight.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady as market stays tight.

text.p: Interbank rates were mostly steady on Monday as liquidity remained tight despite a rumoured injection of funds by the central bank ahead of the weekend, dealers said on Monday.
They said interbank rates were unchanged after recovering from a mild dip in the morning.
"There is no new liquidity in the system. So, rates are still there, unchanged," said the head of money dealing at a Malaysian bank in Kuala Lumpur.
He said there was rumour of some fund injections by Bank Negara on Friday. "They are said to have lent one-month money through their agents, but there is no confirmation" he said.
There was no confirmation from Bank Negara Malaysia, which does not comment on its open market operations.
One-week to three-week money was at 9.0 percent, one-month at 8.4/5 percent and three-month at 8.10/20 percent, all unchanged from Friday.
The overnight was also expected to remain unchanged around 9.0 percent.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mixed, futures dealers said.
At 0415 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down four points to 92.07, or an implied yield of 7.93 percent.
March 1998 contract was down one to 92.38, or 7.62 percent.
Futures dealers said the near month contracts were expected to face more selling pressure because of firm underlying interest rates.
